name: fedify
why: A toolchain for ActivityPub's federated social protocol is a real door into a protocol most people never look at.

brief.what_it_is: fedify is a command-line toolchain from the Fedify project, used for building ActivityPub federated server apps and for debugging ActivityPub servers in general. Its main job is fedify lookup: you give it an object URL or an actor handle such as @user@example.com, and it fetches and prints the ActivityPub object, as a readable dump, compacted or expanded JSON-LD, or raw JSON. It also scaffolds new Fedify projects with fedify init, and runs fedify inbox, a temporary public ActivityPub inbox for watching what your server sends out. The sample config file also has relay and nodeinfo sections, but I did not see the commands for those in the text I read.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the fedify command is a CLI toolchain for Fedify and for debugging ActivityPub-enabled federated server apps. It is primarily aimed at developers who use Fedify, but it says it works with any ActivityPub-enabled server.
brief.how_it_works: For lookup, the tool fetches the URL or resolves the handle over HTTP, then parses the JSON-LD and prints it in the chosen format. With -a/--authorized-fetch, it generates a one-time key pair, starts a temporary ActivityPub server to publish the public key, and signs the request. For fedify inbox, it starts an ephemeral server with a one-time actor, exposes it through a short-lived public DNS name with HTTPS, and logs incoming activities to the console.

commands_seen.context: Installs the CLI globally from npm (also available with bun install -g @fedify/cli).
Homebrew install on macOS and Linux.
Starts the interactive prompt to scaffold a new Fedify project in a new directory.
Previews the files and dependencies that would be created, without writing anything.
Looks up a Note object by its URL and prints it.
Looks up an actor by handle; the @ prefix is optional.
Fetches a protected object by signing the request with a temporary key pair and server, after a plain lookup failed.
Walks an outbox collection and outputs the objects inside it instead of the collection itself.
Loads an extra TOML config file, which takes the highest precedence.
Starts an ephemeral ActivityPub inbox server on a public HTTPS address that stays up until you press ^C.

brief.install_notes: Several routes are documented: npm or Bun (npm install -g @fedify/cli), Homebrew (brew install fedify), Scoop on Windows (scoop install fedify), Deno (deno install -gA --unstable-fs --unstable-kv -n fedify jsr:@fedify/cli, with --unstable-temporal added on Deno versions before 2.7.0), mise (mise use -g github:fedify-dev/fedify), or a pre-built executable from the GitHub releases page placed on your PATH. There is no hardware or account requirement mentioned. Configuration is optional TOML: system-wide, ~/.config/fedify/config.toml (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME), a project-level .fedify.toml, or a file passed with --config. Config needs Fedify 2.0.0 or later, and command-line flags override it.
brief.standout: Two things stand out. fedify inbox gives you a throwaway public ActivityPub actor and inbox, so you can see exactly what your server sends. The lookup command's authorized fetch tries RFC 9421 and falls back to draft-cavage HTTP Signatures (double-knocking), and it also resolves FEP-ef61 portable objects (ap:// URIs with DIDs). Most ActivityPub tooling does not do any of these.
brief.status: Maintained. The GitHub releases page shows Fedify 2.4.4 marked Latest, with a release date of 12 October (2026 in the page text). Patch releases for the 2.0 to 2.4 lines went out within the same few days, and the release notes describe security fixes with advisory IDs. I did not check the commit log directly.
brief.caveats: The homepage text I read was cut off at roughly 40,000 characters, partway through the fedify inbox section, so I did not see the rest of the inbox section, the relay section, or nodeinfo. I also could not read the GitHub repository README, which returned only a path string, so the package-level README was not checked. Authorized fetch and inbox both need a temporary server exposed to the public internet through a tunnel service (fedify.com.es, serveo.net, or pinggy.io are named). Deno installs need the --unstable flags. Release archives are large: roughly 170 to 260 MB for the desktop builds on the releases page. Licence was not visible in what I read.
quotes: The fedify command is a CLI toolchain for Fedify and debugging ActivityPub-enabled federated server apps.
Although it is primarily designed for developers who use Fedify, it can be used with any ActivityPub-enabled server.
Although the given URIs and handle are short-lived, they are anyway publicly dereferenceable until the server is terminated.
